text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 9 in history.
1074 - Pope Gregory VII declared all married Roman Catholic priests to be excommunicated.
1454 - Amerigo Vespucci, Italian explorer who made many voyages to the New World, born. The name of the continent of America was derived from his name.
1796 - Napoleon Bonaparte married Josephine de Beauharnais, widow of a former French officer executed during the revolution.
1831 - The French Foreign Legion was founded by King Louis Philippe with its headquarters in Algeria.
1846 - The First Sikh war ended when Kashmir was ceded to the British East India Company by the Treaty of Lahore.
1864 - General Ulysses S. Grant was appointed commander-in-chief of the Union armies.
1888 - Wilhelm I, former emperor of Germany, died. He was also king of prussia from 1861.
1890 - Vyacheslav Mikhailovich Molotov, Soviet prime minister and foreign secretary, born. He negotiated the non-agression pact with Germany in August 1939.
1916 - Germany declared war on Portugal on grounds that Portugal had seized German shipping in Portuguese harbours.
1918 - Frank Wedekind, German actor and dramatist, died. His brand of satire often roused controversy which led to him being imprisoned for a time.
1924 - Italy annexed the independent city of Fiume but abandoned claims to Yugoslavia's Dalmatian coast.
1932 - Eamon de Valera was appointed president of Ireland.
1932 - Emperor Pu Yi, who had abdicated the Chinese throne in 1912, was installed as president of Japanese-controlled Manchuria.
1943 - Bobby Fischer, world chess champion, born. In 1972 he became the first American to win the world chess championship when he beat Boris Spassky of the Soviet Union in Reykjavik.
1945 - The U.S. 1st Army captured Bonn in World War Two.
1956 - Archbishop Makarios, who the British suspected of terrorism, was deported from Cyprus to the Seychelles.
1970 - A week after Rhodesia became a self-styled republic, the U.S. announced it was to close its consulate in Salisbury.
1976 - 42 skiers were killed when a cable car plunged to the ground in the Italian Dolomites.
1982 - Charles Haughey was sworn in as Irish prime minister.
1991 - Yugoslavia deployed tanks in the capital Belgrade after bloody clashes between riot police and tens of thousands of anti-communist protesters.

1992 - Former Israeli prime minister Menachem Begin died. Once a member of the Irgun Zvai Leumi resistance group and a hardliner concerning the Arabs, he won the Nobel peace prize in 1978 for his part in the Camp David settlement with President Anwar Sadat of Egypt.
1994 - Twenty-six political parties confirmed they would contest South Africa's April election.
1994 - Five Irish Republican Army mortar bombs landed on the runway at London's Heathrow airport but failed to explode.
1994 - Spanish actor Fernando Rey, who starred in "The French Connection" and the films of Luis Bunuel, died aged 76.
1996 - Suspected Moslem guerrillas killed 10 people and wounded 16 when they ambushed a passenger train in western Algeria.
1996 - George Burns, one of America's best loved and most enduring entertainers, died less than two months after celebrating his 100th birthday.
